title: Disquisitionem Iuridicam Inauguralem De Foenore Nautico (Feltz, 1700)
shelf_note: No tradition or collection is assigned. This is a Strasbourg-style law dissertation on maritime loans (foenus nauticum); it belongs in the general early-modern scholarship corpus, not an esoteric shelf.
structure_note: 24 pages, all with OCR and translation. Printed page numbers match the record (image 7 = p.5, 13 = p.11, 18 = p.16). The title string ends 'Ann. MDC' (truncated; published is 1700).

title: Sermonum ... ad populum (Hus, [Strassburg: Schott, ca. 1525])
shelf_note: No tradition is assigned. This is a pre-Reformation/Hussite polemic printed for the early Reformation; it fits a religious-history shelf.
structure_note: The running heads on the sampled pages ('rum carnalium abominatione', 'De Sacerdotum & Monacho[rum]') belong to the tract 'De sacerdotum et monachorum carnalium abominatione', not to sermons 'ad populum'. The volume is probably a compilation, and the record title names only one of its works. 163 pages: 162 OCR, 159 translated.

book_verdict: A good scan, and the OCR is mostly sound. On abbreviation-heavy early print it makes meaning-changing misreads: 'fumorum' for 'summorum', a wrong chapter number, and 'in tolerantia' for 'ob intolerantiam', which reverses an argument. The translation follows these misreads fluently. The record title probably names only one work of a compilation.

title: Assertiones physiologicae de generica differentia partium humani corporis (Bokelius / Balber, Wittenberg)
shelf_note: A Wittenberg disputation on Galen's Ars parva; it fits an early-modern medicine/science shelf.
structure_note: The catalogue says place 'Berlin' and published 'Unknown', but the title says it was disputed at Wittenberg ('Berlin' is the holding library, SBB). The display title runs two names together ('CorneliusBalber'). Image 7 is a handwritten contents list of a bound volume of tracts (items 37–42), not part of this disputation: the record includes flyleaf matter from a volume of bound tracts. Only 13 of 22 pages are translated.

ocr_errors.problem: fragments of the neighbouring page read as marginalia; they are carried into the translation
initial letter of the name is uncertain; it may be F

other.note: a handwritten later-owner contents list of a bound volume of tracts, served as page 7 of this disputation and translated as text

book_verdict: The printed theses are transcribed and translated accurately. The record is untidy: the catalogue has the wrong place (Berlin for Wittenberg), no date and a run-together display title. Flyleaf manuscript leaves from the bound volume are served as pages, and their neighbour-edge letter fragments are read as marginalia.

title: Origenis opera omnia, Tomus primus (1743)
shelf_note: The De la Rue Latin edition of Origen (De principiis, Contra Celsum); patristic Platonism belongs among the library's adjacent traditions.
structure_note: 541 pages: 522 OCR, 517 translated. Printed page numbers match (image 142 = p.104, 276 = p.238, 407 = p.369).

ocr_errors.problem: long s read as f in names throughout, while other words keep ſ correctly; this hurts search on 'Celsus' and 'Jesu'

tr_errors.source: e Aristocreonti.) Niceonti Plutarch. lib. de Virtute moral.
tr_errors.english: e. To Aristocreon. Mentioned by Plutarch, in the book On Moral Virtue
tr_errors.problem: the note's content, that Plutarch names the tyrant differently (Nicocreon), is dropped

other.note: the footnotes a–f are rendered as <margin> blocks in the translation

book_verdict: A dense two-column 1743 edition, read well. The text, apparatus and footnotes are all present and the translations are faithful. The weak points are long-s misread as f in names on one page and a footnote whose point (a variant name) is lost in English. Small type limits word-level certainty.

title: Theologica theoremata ex celebri illa D. Pauli ... (Stevartius / Katzmair, Ingolstadt 1597)

structure_note: 14 pages, all OCR'd and translated. The printed page numbers run 2, 3, 5 across images 4, 7 and 11. The gap between images 4 and 7 is wider than one printed page, so there may be interleaved blanks or plates; nothing looks broken.
